posts.cooked:
Mint, 8/7/19/15/10. I used TakeWalker’s hint about Fueled Freeze (which actually requires Bolster Allies and then an Onboard Module Installation play to get it out in round 1), then I focused on giving Tachyon as many draws and plays as possible to let me pull Hypersonic Assaults and finish with a Lightspeed Barrage/Blitz combo, which I did in round 5 despite a bunch of misplays that I didn’t want to take back in case I actually could pull off a Mint. posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
Finally got it on my 4th try, using the Bolster -> Onboard Module -> Fuel Freeze start. Feels like cheesing it, knowing that a particular sequence changes the card draw to get something important, but this has been so over the top brutal I don’t care.

Legacy really must play Next Evolution / Lead from the Front ASAP after the round 1 (and the first Flechette card). In game 3 I lost because I delayed that a round unintentionally. Other than that, this is all Tachyon’s show.

Wraith really needs to use her base power constantly to feed Tachyon card draws, even though she’s got stuff that’s normally more useful. Tachyon needs to draw Hypersonic Assault again, and that requires a lot of draws. Putting burst cards into Tachyon’s trash is the 2nd most important priority, higher than anything Absolute Zero, Wraith, or Bunker can do.

It’s also worth playing Research Grant and using it instead of Blitz, just because every burst card in her trash is 4-5 damage when it comes time to take down Omnitron. Once her trash burst count is Omnitron’s HP / 4, it’s time to unload with Lightspeed Barrages.

Tachyon’s Synapic Interruption is your only defense against Electropulse Explosives if she doesn’t have a Hypersonic Assault to play.

Part of the reason Wraith needn’t bother setting up is that 2x Technological Singularity is going to wipe equipment. Playing equipment is thus a low-priority task for her, something she should do only if there’s nothing else. She can freely discard equipment to feed Tachyon card draws because she’s not going to play most of it.

Bunker needs one weapon out, otherwise he shouldn’t bother with equipment either.

Absolute Zero can’t do much without the Transducer, so he has to play that. Beyond that it’s Cold Snap and Impales. The Null Point Calibration module only comes out if he’s doesn’t have one shots to play. I did do some self-healing with his cold damage instead of hitting Omnitron, just because I have a hard time letting heroes die. He did manage to make it to the end.

posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
I don't think there's any problem with using AZ's power round 1. You're trading 2 of AZ's health for 2 damage to Omnitron. Which is pretty much standard for AZ, he frequently trades health 1:1 with villain cards, mainly because he can usually get his health back later. Sure, you lose whatever Ongoing you chose, but since it comes from your deck, not your hand, all you're doing is moving a card from your draw pile to your trash.

If you're aiming to incap AZ to use his incap power, the lost health is beneficial. I didn't play it that way, but you could.

But yeah, otherwise the only other ongoing you might want to play round 1 is Pushing the Limits. I regularly play that even if I don't intend to keep it, since it replaces itself. You get a card play and an extra card draw out of it even if you lose it immediately.

posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
Freedom 5 Tachyon gets more out of Research Grant than basic Tachyon IMHO.

It’s true that F5 Tachyon will sometimes forgo Research Grant for Blitz because she needs damage now, or wants to finish off a target and is willing to burn Burst cards to do it. Basic Tachyon never uses Rapid Recon if she can use Research Grant.

However, F5 Tachyon gets more benefit from trashed Burst cards than basic Tachyon. Skipping Blitz one turn gives up 1 damage, plus any damage bonuses. A Burst card trashed by Research Grant is worth that same 1 damage in a later Blitz, plus a card draw, plus 1 damage to every Lightspeed Barrage.

posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
Synaptic Interruption counters the electro-bombs. Choose Tachyon as the first target, and then redirect the blast back to the bomb, destroying it. If you’re making a point of feeding all of Wraith’s cards to Tachyon via her base power, you’ll draw the interruptions before the bombs hit.

While normally I’m a huge fan of the Infrared Eyepiece, I think it’s nigh useless against a flipped Cosmic Omnitron and actually harmful for this particular match. The problem is those chain drone plays. The strength of the eyepiece is delay, and putting a drone on top doesn’t delay anything. So often the eyepiece has you putting a drone on the bottom and accepting a strong villain card as the top card.

In this particular match the 2nd Flechettes card pretty much ends the game, and it’s buried nearly at the bottom of the deck. Every time you use the eyepiece you reduce the number of cards Omnitron has to play until it reaches it. I found this out the hard way.

What you really need is a card that lets you discard from the villain’s deck, like Parse’s Extrasensory Awareness or Buffer Overflow.

posts.name: QuirkyDM
posts.cooked:
Mint for me. Negating Omnitron's damage seemed liked the order of the day, so I focused on going through Tachyon's deck to get Hypersonic Assaults. I saved Bolster Allies until the second turn so Wraith had used her power first. Wraith throat jabbed on turn 1. Tachyon used Hypersonic Assault on the next 3 turns. The only damage taken after turn 1 was when an S-84 Automaton Drone popped up.

Wraith used her power exclusively to give Tachyon card draws. I did play Infrared Eyepiece, but only to use alongside Utility Belt. This meant I could use her card drawing power an extra time every turn.

Legacy gave Tachyon the extra card play every turn except turn 2, where he got rid of the Self-Destruct Sequence.

Absolute Zero really just kept putting out equipment and doing extra damage when he could.

Bunker made sure he always had a gun out, which helps if you get Turret Mode out. Otherwise, he kept playing the cards off the top of Tachyon's deck and he did throw out an Adhesive Grenade.

Tachyon blazed through her deck, using Research Grant and Pushing the Limits liberally. By the time I ran out of Hypersonic Assaults, there were 18 burst cards in her discard, so 3 Lightning Barrages and her base power finished the job easily.

The only thing I would have done different was wait to play Legacy's Inspiring Presence until I was ready to use Tachyon's burst power. I also would have discarded Synaptic Interruption instead of her other bursts since I could get the other bursts into the discard pile by playing them.

And those Hypersonic Assaults are being used in the meantime, so you wouldn’t even need that much. Omnitron was at 70 when I went to town with Tachyon, and I didn’t have boosts from Legacy or AZ.

I’m also thinking that if you really focused, you could keep Omnitron on his front side by doing less than 7 damage per turn. With Throat Jab and Hypersonic Assault, you can ignore the components because all the damage comes from Omnitron.

I ended up with a ludicrous near-mint win, based on the following strategy:

Legacy gives Tachyon card plays, which she uses for her bursts that draw cards.

AZ does his thing and tries not to die.

Wraith goes in for maximum card draw, and uses her funding to funnel it all to Tachyon.

Bunker uses his power to give Tachyon extra top-decks.

Tachyon draws enough cards to use Hypersonic Assault literally every turn for the whole game.

posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
I tried out the "rely entirely on Throat Jab / Hypersonic Assault" strategy, and yeah, it works.

Round 1 Throat Jab.

Round 2 Inspiring Presence, Hypersonic Assault.

Rounds 3-4 Hypersonic Assault.

Round 5, Tachyon has drawn her entire deck, 17 Burst cards in the trash, 2x Lightspeed Barrage is enough to finish Omnitron off. No need to use Blitz.

Clearly, while Tachyon does a lot of the damage, the other heroes piled on quite a bit since Omnitron is at about 30 HP at the start of round 5. An early Inspiring Presence helps, as does taking down the adaptive platings with 2x Blazing Speed.

I didn't draw Fueled Freeze this time, which is OK, since Tachyon playing Blazing Speed adds burst cards to her trash.

Rounds 1 and 2 I kept my overall damage low to avoid destroying the components and flipping Omnitron. Round 3 I found that I'd piled on enough damage that Hypersonic Assault was going to trigger it. This does delay Omnitron a little, so only one Tech Singularity comes out.

Bunker used his base power rounds 1-3, whereas in my earlier game he'd draw a cannon and fired away with it. This gave Tachyon a couple of plays (once I declined to play her card because it was an early Lightspeed Barrage).

Final HP was Legacy 13, Absolute Zero 2, Wraith 16, Tachyon 9, Bunker 11. Absolute Zero's health is low almost entirely because of self-harm. Tachyon took quite a few hits while drawing cards, prior to Throat Jab and in between Throat Jab and Hypersonic Assault.
